title: Comparison Constant Limit at Zero
statement: For each real number $\lambda$, define $C(\lambda)=e$ when $\lambda=1/2$ and $C(\lambda)=((1-\lambda)/\lambda)^{1/(2(1-2\lambda))}$ otherwise, with real powers interpreted using the usual real-power convention. As $\lambda$ tends to $0$ through positive values, $C(\lambda)\sqrt{\lambda}$ tends to $1$.
